usageNotes: Use this to retrieve paginated log output for any task identified by its UPID — most useful for polling a running task or inspecting a completed one. Obtain the UPID from the operation that launched the task (e.g. a backup, migration, or sync job). Use `start` + `limit` for pagination through large logs, or set `limit=0` to return all lines; pass `download=true` exclusively (without any other params) to stream the raw log file.

examples.summary: Fetch the first 100 lines of a task log on the local PDM node

tips: Set `test-status: true` to check whether the task is still running alongside the log fetch — avoids a separate status call.
When paginating, use the `total` field in the response to know when you have fetched all lines.
`download=true` cannot be combined with `start`, `limit`, or `test-status` — it triggers a raw file download instead of JSON.
The UPID encodes the originating node; always route the request to that same node, not a different cluster member.
